questions.question: If cargo with hazardous materials is leaking, what should the driver do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone and alert emergency personnel
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility
Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel
Continue driving to the destination

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel
questions.explanation: If hazardous materials leak, do not drive any longer than needed for safety. Continuing to drive spreads contamination. Instead, park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and send someone for help.

questions.question: Hazardous materials rules protect all of the following, except:

options.text: You
People around you
The environment
Buildings

questions.correctAnswerText: Buildings
questions.explanation: Governments at federal, state, and local levels create rules for transporting hazardous materials. These rules protect the driver, people nearby, and the environment.

questions.question: When accepting hazardous materials, a driver should check that:

options.text: The shipping papers match the markings and labels on packages
The shipping papers are written in code
All packages are labeled as poison
All boxes are sealed

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping papers match the markings and labels on packages
questions.explanation: When carrying hazardous materials, compare the shipping papers to the markings and labels on the packages.

questions.question: Some areas have restrictions on transporting explosives or hazardous waste. What should you do about these restrictions?

options.text: They usually are not a concern
They do not apply on weekends
Research them before choosing your route
They only apply to shipments over 1,000 pounds

questions.correctAnswerText: Research them before choosing your route
questions.explanation: Before transporting hazardous materials, research any restrictions that apply to the routes you plan to take.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be kept while you are driving?

options.text: Within easy reach
In the sleeping compartment
Hidden under the seat
Taped to the passenger window

questions.correctAnswerText: Within easy reach
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in another place you can easily reach while wearing your seatbelt. Papers must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Who can transport hazardous materials?

options.text: Any driver with a CDL
Any driver if the hazardous materials weigh under 50 pounds
Any driver in a rural area
A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and HazMat endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: What can you do with an improperly placarded vehicle?

options.text: It can never be moved
It can only be moved in an emergency
It can be driven short distances
It can be driven if it does not contain radioactive materials

questions.correctAnswerText: It can only be moved in an emergency
questions.explanation: A hazardous materials vehicle must have proper placards to be driven. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be driven in an emergency to protect life or property.

questions.question: How many placards must a vehicle carrying hazardous materials have?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: A vehicle with hazardous materials must display at least four identical placards. Place them on the front, back, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What must you do to complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest?

options.text: Sign it by hand
Sign it only if you cross into another state
Sign it only if weather conditions were hazardous
Have a witness sign it

questions.correctAnswerText: Sign it by hand
questions.explanation: A Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest must be signed by hand. Include the names and EPA registration numbers of shippers, carriers, and the destination on the manifest.

questions.question: A person supervising tank loading or unloading must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay alert
Stay within 25 feet of the tank
Wear a chemical suit
Know the hazards of the materials

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a chemical suit
questions.explanation: A supervisor overseeing tank loading or unloading must stay alert, keep a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards involved, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank.

questions.question: If required, how many identical placards must be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: Two
Four
Six
Eight

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials placards are required, place four identical placards on the vehicle. Put one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: On a shipping paper, if the letter "G" appears in Column 1, what else must be listed?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material
The type of packaging containing the hazardous material
The shipper's phone number
The date the product was packed

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material
questions.explanation: If the letter "G" (for "Generic") appears in Column 1 of a shipping paper, you must also list the technical name of the hazardous material.

questions.question: What must emergency response information include?

options.text: Risks of fire or explosion
Value of the materials
Driver information
Planned route

questions.correctAnswerText: Risks of fire or explosion
questions.explanation: Emergency response information for hazardous materials must include details about fire and explosion risks.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of hazardous materials shipping papers?

options.text: Five months
One year
Two years
10 years

questions.correctAnswerText: Two years
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy of shipping papers for at least two years from the date the material is handed to the first carrier. For hazardous waste, keep them for three years.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be placed in a trailer with:

options.text: A heater
An air conditioner
Other items
Paper

questions.correctAnswerText: A heater
questions.explanation: Heaters are not allowed when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: How should containers of nitric acid be stacked?

options.text: No more than two containers high
Stacked to the ceiling
Loaded on top of other products
Loaded in the cabin

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than two containers high
questions.explanation: Stack nitric acid containers no higher than two containers. Do not stack them on top of other products.

questions.question: What should a driver do if given a leaking package of hazardous materials?

options.text: Accept it
Refuse it
Leave it on the side of the road
Get someone else to drive it

questions.correctAnswerText: Refuse it
questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse any leaking packages or shipments of hazardous materials.

questions.question: When do you need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: In a vehicle requiring a Class A license
In a vehicle requiring a Class B license
In a vehicle requiring a Class C license
In any sized vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: In any sized vehicle
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: What license is required to operate a vehicle used to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: Only a CDL
A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a passenger endorsement
A CDL with an air brake endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a commercial driver license with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials, even if it is not currently carrying them.

questions.question: What type of material is classified as Class 7 hazardous material?

options.text: Explosive
Flammable
Radioactive
Corrosive

questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive
questions.explanation: Class 7 hazardous materials are radioactive materials.

questions.question: When must you use a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard?

options.text: When carrying more than 50 pounds of the product.
When carrying more than 10 pounds of the product.
When carrying any amount of the product.
When carrying the product in a non-sealed container.

questions.correctAnswerText: When carrying any amount of the product.
questions.explanation: You must always display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard and the correct hazard class placard. This applies even to small amounts of the material.

questions.question: Where should you NOT keep hazardous materials shipping papers?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's side door
In a pouch on the passenger's side door
Within reach of the driver while wearing a seat belt
On the driver's seat when the driver is outside the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view within the driver's reach while driving. If you leave the vehicle, keep the papers on the driver's seat.

questions.question: What should a carrier do if hazardous materials are not properly prepared?

options.text: Accept the shipment
Accept the shipment and note your concerns
Accept the shipment but write on the paperwork
Refuse the shipment

questions.correctAnswerText: Refuse the shipment
questions.explanation: You must refuse to carry hazardous materials that are not properly prepared.

questions.question: When transporting mass explosives, what must you do?

options.text: Always placard your vehicle.
Placard your vehicle only if carrying more than 200 pounds.
You do not need to placard your vehicle.
Only use rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always placard your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Some hazardous materials only require placards when carrying 1,001 pounds or more. However, mass explosives must be placarded regardless of the amount you are carrying.

questions.question: What must emergency response information from the shipper include?

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
The value of the materials.
Driver information.
How many people should respond in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include the material names; health hazards; fire and explosion risks; accident precautions; fire control methods; spill and leak procedures; and first aid measures.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
Throw water on the doors.
Put on gloves.
Wait 30 minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Always feel the doors before opening them. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. If the doors are hot, keep them closed.

questions.question: If hazardous materials start leaking while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive to a phone booth.
Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
Leave the area to find help.
Drive around looking for someone to fix the leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Stop driving immediately when a leak occurs. Continuing to drive spreads contamination. Park safely, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and send someone else to get help.

questions.question: Should identification numbers, shipping names, and hazard classes be abbreviated on shipping papers?

options.text: Yes, if using a small piece of paper.
Yes, to make them easier to read.
No, never abbreviate them.
Yes, if the abbreviations are easy to understand.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never abbreviate them.
questions.explanation: Never abbreviate identification numbers, shipping names, or hazard classes on shipping papers. The only exception is abbreviations that are specifically allowed in hazardous materials regulations.

questions.question: What do you do if a hazardous material label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Attach the label to a tag secured to the package.
Attach a QR code to the package instead.
Reduce the label size to fit the package.
Paste the label on the trailer wall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag secured to the package.
questions.explanation: If the label does not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: What is a clue that your shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper works in a business that typically handles hazardous materials, like fireworks or pest control.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.
The packaging looks damaged.
The shipper's business is in a bad part of town.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper works in a business that typically handles hazardous materials, like fireworks or pest control.
questions.explanation: Watch for shippers in industries that commonly use hazardous materials. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, and pest control companies.
